title: Capacity To Ship Packages Within D Days
prompt: A conveyor belt has packages that must be shipped from one port to another within `days` days. The i-th package on the conveyor belt has a weight of `weights[i]`. Each day, packages are loaded onto a ship in the order given by `weights`, up to the ship's maximum weight capacity, without reordering the packages. Return the least weight capacity of the ship that will result in all packages being shipped within `days` days.
hints: The capacity must be at least the heaviest single package, and at most the sum of all packages (shipping everything in one day) — that range itself is a hint about how to search.

For a fixed capacity, you can greedily simulate loading: keep adding packages to the current day's load until the next one would exceed capacity, then start a new day. This tells you exactly how many days a given capacity requires.
The number of days required is monotonically non-increasing as capacity increases, so binary search on capacity itself using that simulation as the feasibility check.

solution.approach: Binary search over the possible ship capacities, bounded below by the heaviest package (anything less can never load it) and above by the sum of all weights (shipping everything in a single day). For a candidate capacity, greedily simulate the loading process to count how many days it would take; this day count is monotonically non-increasing as capacity grows, satisfying the binary search invariant. If the simulated days fit within the budget, the capacity is feasible so try smaller; otherwise increase the capacity. This finds the minimum feasible capacity in O(n log(sum of weights)) time.
